questions.q: How does this lesson say the checklist should actually be used?
options: As a working tool run against a real environment, a case study, or a control map — with a specific answer for each item, not just a general 'yes, probably'
As a summary to read once and never revisit
As a replacement for every tool covered earlier in the course
As a legal document that must be notarized
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly says each checklist item should get a specific tool, person, or document as its answer, not a vague impression.

questions.q: Per the Chapter 5 section of this checklist, what two things should a real control map always include?
options: A list of every password used across both clouds
A complete list of every employee's salary
A guarantee that no control will ever need to change
A pairing of each primary-cloud control with its secondary-cloud equivalent, and a named owner for each row
questions.explain: The control map needs both the cross-cloud pairing and an owner — even an honestly 'unassigned' one — to be a real governance tool rather than a document that just looks complete.

questions.q: What is the 'one-search test' this checklist describes?
options: Whether AWS and Azure use the same search bar
Whether you can find a job posting using one search engine
Whether you could answer a regulator's question about who can access a dataset across every system in one search, or whether it would require two separate investigations
Whether your company's website loads in under one second
questions.explain: The one-search test checks whether cross-cloud cataloging (Lesson 22) actually gives a unified answer, rather than requiring separate Azure and AWS investigations.

questions.q: What is this course's single biggest piece of closing advice, per this lesson?
options: Always choose AWS over Azure for every workload
Tools like Entra ID, Azure Policy, AWS IAM, and Purview don't govern anything by themselves — a named owner and a recurring habit are what make governance real
Governance tools are unnecessary if the company is small enough
The most expensive governance tool is always the most effective one
questions.explain: The lesson's closing point is that the tools make good governance possible, but a named owner actually running the review and keeping the control map current is what makes it real.

questions.q: Which course does this lesson name as the next course in the Data Governance career path?
options: Data Governance Program Management
Data Governance Architecture
Snowflake Data Governance
AI & Machine Learning Governance
questions.explain: The lesson's closing section names AI & Machine Learning Governance as the next course, extending governance from data itself to the models trained on it.
